newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE said closer to decision on missiles.
newsitem.headline: UAE said closer to decision on missiles.

text.p: After six years of deliberations, the United Arab Emirates is moving closer to choosing an air defence missile system in a deal potentially worth between $500 million and $1 billion, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"The UAE is moving closer to making a decision," said an industry executive who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Two companies are in the running.

They are American firm Raytheon, whose electronic systems unit has been marketing its Patriot anti-missile missiles and holding talks with military procurement officers in the Gulf Arab state since 1990, and Russian missile maker Antei.
"The Russians have provided all their information on their missiles to the UAE. Additional talks are not expected. They have been completed," said an industry source.

If Raytheon secures Patriot missiles sales to the UAE, or Antei wins an order for Russia's top of the line S-300V tactical surface to air and anti-ballistic missile systems, the deal could be worth up to $1 billion, said the industry sources.
A contract would give Raytheon another foothold in the Gulf, where appetites for high-tech weapons have grown since Iraq's lightning invasion of Kuwait in 1990 raised security fears.
Patriots gained notoriety in the Gulf War when they intercepted Iraqi Scud missiles.
Since then, defence giant Raytheon has sold Saudi Arabia and Kuwait about $3 billion in Patriot systems, industry sources say.

Industry executives say the Patriots would carry a bigger price tag but pointed out that the S-300V system would require greater manpower, and that logistical support networks and spare parts could prove hard to come by if the UAE chooses the Russian missiles.

"The Russians are in need of cash so they are exporting the S-300V and the price will be lower than the Patriot. Traditionally they have not exported their best defence systems but now they need hard currency," said an industry executive.

Russia's chief arms export agency, Rosvooruzheniye, which has launched a drive to catch up with the United States and establish Moscow as the world's chief arms salesman by the end of the century, is marketing the S-300V in Abu Dhabi.
It is not clear when Abu Dhabi, a low-key emirate that has lured major Western arms makers seeking lucrative deals, will decide which missiles to buy.
The UAE is expected to announce several deals at the IDEX arms show on March 16-19, when 700 companies from 45 countries will descend on Abu Dhabi to exhibit their weaponry.
"They could announce a missile decision at IDEX or at some time before the end of the year. You never know in this market," said an industry source.
